subject: How to estimate theta from parameters only?

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: How to estimate theta from parameters only?
parts:
Hello,

I have a data frame with columns containing item parameters:

| itemname |  a  |  b1  |  b2  |  b3  | b4 |
| name1       |  4  | -1.6 | -1.1| -0.2 | 0.6 |
etc.

These parameters are fixed and it is unidimensional data

How can I estimate the theta distributions given these parameters?

I have tried tot run a mirt model, but because alle parameters are fixed, I obviously got an error: Error: Computing ACOV matrix is meaningless when no parameters are estimated. 
I have parsed these values into params$value and the params$est = FALSE. Of course I can set params$est = TRUE to run a mirt model, but I don't think this allowed as it returns a whole new set of parameters?

Some background for my question. I am evaluating an item bank that contains new items. I ran an mirt model with the original params fixed and estimated the params for the new items. Now I also want to compare the theta distribution from this new extended item bank with the original item bank (ie the items with known/fixed parameters).

Can anyone point me in the right direction how to do this in MIRT (or if not possible otherwise in R)?

Sincerly,

Guido

You should only be seeing this message if you passed SE=TRUE, which would be meaningless if all the parameters are being treated as a fixed and known.

I have parsed these values into params$value and the params$est = FALSE. Of course I can set params$est = TRUE to run a mirt model, but I don't think this allowed as it returns a whole new set of parameters?
You could, see the TOL argument as it accepts inputs such as NA and NaN, which do different things.

Some background for my question. I am evaluating an item bank that contains new items. I ran an mirt model with the original params fixed and estimated the params for the new items. Now I also want to compare the theta distribution from this new extended item bank with the original item bank (ie the items with known/fixed parameters).

You could try mirt::fixedCalib(), which sounds a lot like what you are trying to do. HTH.

Phil
